newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Cimpor sale oversubscribed nearly fivefold.
newsitem.headline: Cimpor sale oversubscribed nearly fivefold.

text.p: Applications for shares in the public offer for sale (OPV) of Portuguese cement producer Cimpor outstripped supply almost fivefold at the end of pre-registration, a source familiar with the process said.
The source said on Monday applications for more than 75 million shares had been received at the end of pre-registration last Friday for the 16 million available in the OPV.
"The strong demand is due to the financial solidity of the group and falling interest rates," the source told Reuters.
Lisbon bourse will announce the results of the privatisation of a 45 percent stake in Cimpor-Cimentos de Portugal, Portugal's biggest cement producer, on October 15.
Portugal's Socialist government plans to sell 16 million shares in the OPV and 18.96 million by direct sale.

The OPV is divided into four groups -- employees, small investors and emigrants, existing shareholders (who hold shares acquired before September 6 and retain them until the end of the OPV), and the general public.
Cimpor employees have been allocated 600,000 shares, small investors and emigrants 12 million, shareholders 1.2 million and the general public 2.2 million.
The previous Social Democrat government sold a 20 percent stake in Cimpor.
The total number of shares for sale may be increased by up to 15 percent if there is strong demand in the privatisation.
Investors may submit orders this week. An international road show to promote the sale proceeds until next Friday.
